10

  • N: ašši | rēšīya || ana sîn | akarrab
  • T: I lifted my head, praying to Sîn,
  • L: ašši ← našû II “to lift, carry”; rēšīya ← rēšu I “head”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; sîn ← Sîn I “the moon(-god) Bab., M/NA”; akarrab ← karābu II “to pray, bless, greet”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "IX" 24
NinNA1 i 10. [x x re]-ši-ia# a-na {d}30 a-kar-rab
NinNA2 i 10. aš₂-ši re-š[i-ia x x x x x x x]

11

  • N: ana [ ... | na]mirti? (|) ilī || illakū | supûʾa
  • T: to [ … , the] light of the gods, my supplications went:
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; na]mirti? ← nawirtu I “brightness, light O/jB n. šakānu to bring about brightness”; ilī ← ilu I “pl. ilū, ilānu god, deity a or the god, also du.”; illakū ← alāku I “to go”; supûʾa ← supû I “prayer, supplication M/NB to deity, esp. s. teslīti, s. sulû etc.”
  • Note: See [RN117: 862]: “The trace after a-na is not certainly DI[NGIR], either here or in the apparent parallel l. 25, but the indirect object of illikū suppûʾa is very likely a deity. The plural imperative šullimāʾinni in l. 12 presupposes that more than one deity was invoked, and thus rules out a repetition of {d}sîn from l. 10. As the most prominent of the astral deities, Venus is perhaps the foremost candidate for restoration here, but this is uncertain while the trace before šullimāʾinni in l. 12 is undeciphered. (…) If it is right to restore a divine name following ana, there is not room enough in the break also to accommodate the standard epithet šākin(at) namirti (used of both Sîn and Šamaš, and also the fire god: see CAD N/1, p. 229). As a provisional solution I propose simply DN namirti.”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "IX" 25
NinNA1 i 11. [x x x x x na?]-mir#?-ti# DINGIR-MEŠ DU-ku su-pu-u-a
NinNA2 i 11. a-na {d#?}[x x x x x x x x x x x x x]

  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "IX" 26
NinNA1 i 12. [x x x x] x šul-li-ma-in-ni ia-a-ti

  • L: mut[tiš] ← muttiš I “in front, before (s.o.) O/jB”; sîn ← Sîn I “the moon(-god) Bab., M/NA”; ihtedu ← hadû III “to be joyful, rejoice”; balāṭu ← balāṭu I “life esp. ana balāṭ X for X's life”

  • T: He took up his axe in his hand,

16

  • N: išlup | [namṣār] | šibbīšu
  • T: he drew forth [the dirk from] his belt.
  • L: išlup ← šalāpu I “to pull out, draw, unsheathe”; [namṣār] ← namṣāru I; šibbīšu ← šibbu I “belt Bab. (sword-)belt”
  • Note: See [RN117: 862]: “In l. 16 the break does not seem to be wide enough to accommodate namṣara ina, which is the phrasing expected from the only versions of this line that survives unbroken (OB Ishchali, Nergal and Ereskigal), and the big area of blank clay before šibbīšu suggests that there was no preposition on this occasion. Consequently namṣaru is restored in construct state.”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "Ischchali" 21'

37

  • N: ša šadî | šemūšu | māš[u(m)-ma]
  • T: The name of the mountain was Māšu.
  • L: ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; šadî ← šadû I “st. constr. šad(i)”; šemūšu ← šumu I “pl. m., also -ānu”; māš[u(m)-ma] ← mašû I “f. mašītu(m)”
  • Note: See [RN117: 863]: “The spelling še-mu for šumu was understood by von Soden as standing for šᵉmu (AHw, pp. 1274–5). However, according to I.J. Gelb šumu derives from older *šimum (BiOr 12 (1955), p.105; cf. Hebrew šēm), so this orthography might instead derive from an archaic or dialectal variant of the word. (…) Perhaps, in the end, the text will turn out to be corrupt (read <<ŠE>> šum₃-su₂). However that may be, the singular possessive suffix here and in l. 42 (bābšu, unless the referent there is the sun) is at first glance difficult to reconcile with the plural possessive suffixes in ll. 40-1 (elūšunu, irassunu). The solution proposed is that the Twin Mountains were indeed two mountains, one in the west and one in the east (such is the clear implication of l. 45). The singular pronouns refer to the mountain Gilgameš has reached, the plural to the mountains as a pair. (…)”
NinNA1 ii 1. ša₂ ša-di-i še-mu-šu₂ ma-š[u-(um)-ma]

NinNA1 ii 2. ana ša-ad ma-a-ši i-na ka-š[a₂-di-šu]

  • Note: On the mountain of sunrise, see [RN117: 863–864].
